title: Transitivity conjecture for the Galois action on enharmonic functions
statement: Let $G$ be a graph with boundary, and suppose the energies and boundary values are rational, with positive energies. Let $\Sigma_u$ denote the set of compatible orientations, equivalently the enharmonic functions supplied by Theorem A, and let $\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}^{tr}/\mathbb{Q})$ act on $\Sigma_u$ through its action on the corresponding algebraic solutions. A graph with boundary is **3-connected** if, after adding edges connecting every pair of boundary vertices, it cannot be disconnected by removing two vertices. **Transitivity conjecture.** If $G$ is 3-connected, the above Galois action is transitive for generic rational energies and boundary data, where generic means on a Zariski open set. This predicts that the algebraic enharmonic functions form a single orbit under the totally real Galois group in the 3-connected case; the conjecture is presented without a resolution in the source.
source_name: Aaron Abrams and Richard Kenyon, “Fixed-energy harmonic functions”, arXiv:1505.05785 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.05785

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).
